topics.title: Git Architecture: Working Tree, Index & Commit Graph
topics.objective: Understand repository initialization, staging files, committing snapshots, and viewing commit history.
topics.example: git init && git add . && git commit -m "feat: initial commit"
topics.exercise: Initialize a local repository, create tracking commits, and inspect git log and git status.

topics.title: Branching & Fast-Forward Merging
topics.objective: Create, checkout, and merge isolated feature branches without disrupting mainline history.
topics.example: git checkout -b feature/login && git merge main
topics.exercise: Create two parallel branches, implement distinct features, and merge them into main.

topics.title: Merge Conflicts & 3-Way Diff Resolution
topics.objective: Identify conflict marker sections (<<<<<<<, =======, >>>>>>>) and resolve overlapping edits cleanly.
topics.example: git status # shows unmerged paths; git add resolved_file.txt
topics.exercise: Simulate a merge conflict across two branches and manually resolve the divergence.

topics.title: Remotes, Fetching, Pulling & Upstream Tracking
topics.objective: Connect local repositories to remote forges (GitHub/GitLab) and synchronize branch pointers.
topics.example: git remote add origin <url> && git push -u origin main
topics.exercise: Configure an upstream remote repository and sync divergent commits using git pull --rebase.

topics.title: Interactive Rebase, Stashing & Commit Sanitization
topics.objective: Squash messy WIP commits, stash transient work in progress, and write Conventional Commit messages.
topics.example: git rebase -i HEAD~3 # pick, squash, reword
topics.exercise: Clean up a 5-commit exploratory feature branch into 2 atomic commits following Conventional Commits.
